title: Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was the son of Rav Chisda, Rav Sheshet’s colleague, as in Tosafot on Bava Batra 141a, s.v. Uledidi. Hyman infers that Rav Chisda named his son after the son’s maternal grandfather, Rav Chanan bar Rava, as in Avodah Zarah 11b and Chullin 63a, where his father said to him, “Thus said your mother’s father,” etc. He received from his father, as in Avodah Zarah 11b, where he asked his father. In Shabbat 48a, Rav Chanan bar [Rav, Dikdukei Soferim] Chisda raised an objection to Rav Chisda; and in Moed Katan 25a he raised an objection to his father, and his father struck him with his sandal.

He is mentioned in halakhah in Avodah Zarah 16a: “Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda said — and some say Rav Chanan bar Rava,” which Hyman explains as a doubt whether Rav Chanan bar Rava said it or his grandson. There, 11b: “Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda said that Rav said — and some say Rav Chanan bar Rava said that Rav said.” Hyman suggests the reading “Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda said — and some say Rav Chanan bar Rava,” and an extra “Rav said” crept in; or, he proposes, it should read as in Chullin 63a, “Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda said that Rav Chisda said.” Yuchasin cites from Bava Batra 8a: “Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda imposed a head-tax on the Rabbis; Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to him: You have transgressed,” etc., and so is Dikdukei Soferim’s reading. But Hyman prefers his received reading, Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda, for we find that Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda was the head in the town of Drukart, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak too was there, as in Taanit 21b; but we do not find that Rav Chanan his brother was head in his town — unless, he suggests, we say that Rav Chanan and Rav Nachman are one name.

notes.text: Named after his maternal grandfather is Hyman’s inference from the quoted your mother’s father, not RavChisda’s own maternal grandfather. His proposed removal of אמר רב, preference for Nachman and possible Chanan/Nachman equivalence remain competing proposals, without identity binding.

The consulted Chullin 63a directly names Chanan bar Chisda reporting Chisda and Chanan son of Rava; the next paragraph says your mother’s father. This preserves the son’s maternal-grandfather direction. Hyman’s correction of אמר רב, Chanan/Nachman alternatives and Drukart chronology are not resolved into a new identity binding.
